brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A tartary buckwheat infusion from Liangshan prefecture in Sichuan, sold as granulated tea or as whole or broken grain.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: Development began in the prefecture in 1997. By 2012 more than 30 producers were active, and local regulators set a standard and licensing rules that year. Geographical indication protection followed on 23 January 2013, covering all of Liangshan.
processing: Dried plant material, as with most herbal infusions.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
appearance_dry: Granulated tea is yellow-brown, yellow-green or black-brown; whole-grain tea is round or broken kernels.
taste_profile: The characteristic aroma of tartary buckwheat.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
